task: r9t5 - third-party review of t1: is the r9t1 runbook actually followable, not just a retelling of one success
headline: Overall: 成立 (sound), with three info-level notes and no falsification found. The runbook is genuinely followable: every registration step ships an executable command plus the expected output, the browser-context requirement is stated three times, and #manual/#pop are named with a DOM probe. Its three recorded failures are not invented - I hit all three myself, independently, in the same session: the TAB_FAILED PermissionError on default.json, the stale pinned id CEB3AD7543E8B2BEB1F3A9FE26F0BE6A (which my own tab-list printed verbatim at 13:39:57.378Z), and the StandardOutputEncoding capture failure. Steps carry a count at every hop (0,0,0,0,1,1), not just first and last. The new timestamp 13:39:55.037Z differs from all three 12:36/12:37 moments, t53 exited 0 with 5/5, and I reproduced the same six values twice more (13:40:16.452Z and 14:04:06.771Z), so the numbers are not stale substitutions. The one real defect is in step 3: the DOM check it gives tests PRESENCE, while the judgement it asks for is VISIBILITY - I ran the runbook's exact eval at 14:03:45.760Z and it returned manual:true/pop:true/popTag:BUTTON while those elements were hidden=true, offsetParent=null and 0 px wide. It does not invalidate the runbook (section 1.2 already tells a replayer with count=1 not to re-register), but a literal replayer can be told 'present' about an element they cannot click.

findings.title: step 3's DOM probe tests presence, the judgement asks for visibility
findings.detail: L108 runs manual:!!document.querySelector('#manual') and pop:!!document.querySelector('#pop'), then L119 judges '#manual 可见、#pop 存在且是 BUTTON'. querySelector finds a hidden element, so the probe cannot establish visibility. I ran the runbook's exact command at 2026-10-24T14:03:45.760Z on the live landing page and it returned {"manual":true,"pop":true,"popTag":"BUTTON"}, while a visibility probe on the same page at the same moment returned {"manualHiddenAttr":true,"manualOffsetParent":false,"manualRect":0,"popRect":0} - both elements were present and 0 px wide. This is exactly the short-circuit case: when the relay already has a window, the page hides #manual and stops polling, so a literal replayer is told 'present' about an element they cannot click. My own attempt to click it at 13:41:01.131Z failed with '元素不可交互(hidden)'.
findings.whyItIsNotFatal: section 1.2 L59 already tells a replayer whose count is 1 not to re-register, and section 8 warns that /health is not a liveness probe. The defect is in the check's wording and command, not in the procedure's intent.
findings.suggestedFix: change L108 to return manualVisible: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('#manual')).display !== 'none' && document.querySelector('#manual').offsetParent !== null (plus the same for #pop), and change L119 to judge on that field

findings.title: 'about 2 seconds' understates the observed 4.0 s
findings.detail: L269 says '真人点击 #pop 后约 2 秒计数 0 -> 1', and L139 sleeps 2 s, but the recorded samples are click 13:39:33.364Z -> health 13:39:37.358Z, i.e. 3.994 s. The extra time is plausibly the click round trip plus command startup, so the numbers are not contradictory - only the summary's '2 seconds' is optimistic. A replayer should wait and re-poll rather than time out at 2 s.

findings.title: hardcoded tab index 1
findings.detail: L94 and L131 use dpx tab-select 1. In this session the landing tab happened to be index 1, but the index depends on how many tabs the user has open. Selecting by URL fragment (dpx tab-select 49620/landing) works and is stable - I used it when closing the landing tabs. The runbook's L131 advice 'do not reuse the old pinned id' is right; selecting by URL would make it robust.

findings.title: no operational step for opening the editor
findings.detail: L19 treats 'the editor tab is already loaded in the same browser/profile' as a precondition and L38 says to stop otherwise. That is honest but it means the document cannot cold-start a session; it only replays registration onto an editor that is already open.
